the appellant broke the glass door of a public transit bus in the course of a dispute with the bus driver

crime_highlights: The appellant repeatedly sexually assaulted one of the victims and directed other young men to similarly abuse her.
the offences have had a significant and long-lasting emotional impact on both victims
rationale_highlights: The appellant's paternal and maternal grandparents, as well as his father, aunts and uncles, are residential school survivors
The appellant's father was sexually abused while attending a residential school
There can be little doubt that the appellant was living in dysfunctional circumstances when the offences were committed
the appellant's circumstances diminish his moral blameworthiness
note: Appeal court's own finding; result driven mainly by Crown concession

crime_highlights: the appellant, who was intoxicated, entered a residence occupied by four college students through a ground floor bedroom window
She hid in her bedroom closet and contacted the police.
rationale_highlights: His upbringing has properly been characterized as chaotic and highly dysfunctional
He was raised by his maternal great uncle, a residential school survivor, and his wife
The judge in this case recognized that the appellant's moral culpability was reduced as a result of his status as a disadvantaged aboriginal offender who suffers from FASD
I cannot say that the judge committed error in principle or otherwise exercised his discretion in an unreasonable fashion
note: Appeal court endorses trial judge's reduced culpability finding
